settlement_source: United States Congress (Source Agency); in practice party of first-sworn Senator, accelerated via 8 media decision desks
settlement_variable: Party of the first candidate presenting certificate of election and sworn in to the seat for the term beginning in the stated year
timezone: Expiration time 10:00 AM ET; settlement no later than day after Expiration Date
tie_handling: unknown (no tie clause in SENATEPARTY terms; party of first-sworn Senator decides; vacancy -> party of first person sworn as temporary or permanent replacement)
trading_close_vs_settlement: Last Trading Time = Expiration Time. Expiration = sooner of first 10:00 AM ET after swearing-in or 1 year after popular vote; listed close_time (2027-11-03 / 2029-11-07) is a placeholder upper bound. Accelerated determination: >=4 of 8 Designated Media Sources (NYT, AP, DDHQ, CNN, Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC) declare a winner with none contradicting -> early resolution; can_close_early=1, settlement_timer 1800s.
early_close_or_void_clauses: Accelerated resolution on 4/8 media-source consensus with no contradiction
Exchange may replace a Designated Media Source at sole discretion
Kalshi may initiate Market Outcome Review (Rule 6.3(c)) at sole discretion before settlement
Party switch between election and swearing-in: resolves on party at election day
No explicit void clause; no-data fallback is discretionary
title_vs_rules_divergences: Title says 'win the Senate race' but rule is 'sworn in' - resolution can wait for swearing-in (Jan) unless accelerated by media consensus
Title typo 'Democratics'; resolves on Democratic party of sworn Senator
Independent winners: terms specify Independent only by named individual
close_time (Nov 2027) is far after the Nov 3 2026 election; actual expiry is earlier
toxicity_flags: Resolution by media-call consensus (4/8) rather than certified result; wrong-call/contradiction risk
Outcome public minutes before price fully adjusts after poll close; fast news bots / informed flow
Discretionary exchange review and source substitution
Insider prohibitions (campaign staff, decision-desk employees) imply known information asymmetry
Alaska RCV/slow absentee count -> prolonged uncertainty, contradictory-call risk
notes: Rules from SENATEPARTY.pdf. Series maps to SENATEPARTY terms. 2026 election already held as of 2026-11-04 PT; results observable from AP/DDHQ. Alaska uses top-4 RCV general and slow absentee counts; calls may lag, raising contradiction/delay risk. 2028 iteration (SENATEAK-28-D) is thin: 0.26/0.34.
